headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared-bus Pipecat can amplify Argo outputs into downstream actions, while both agents’ allowlisted egress creates moderate leakage and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows has no documented direct ingestion of Pipecat outputs, and Pipecat’s shared bus is not shown to bridge into Argo by default. The only plausible pathway is manual or orchestrated copy/paste or file handoff, so injection risk is limited and not default. Uncertainty remains because neither profile documents provenance controls.
conditions: IF an operator copies Pipecat-generated text into an Argo workflow parameter or file
IF a shared bus message is transformed into an Argo command without validation
mitigations: Use a strict allowlist for any text passed from Pipecat to Argo
Add a human review step before Argo consumes Pipecat output
Strip instruction-like content from shared-bus messages
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and schema validation at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, and Pipecat handles text, audio, video, images, and conversation state. Both have allowlisted network egress, so if they share a workspace or bridge, sensitive artifacts can flow into Pipecat’s external service calls. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default integrations, though not proven from docs alone.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts or parameters contain secrets or regulated data
IF Pipecat is configured to send conversation or media content to third-party STT/LLM/TTS services
mitigations: Keep Argo and Pipecat on separate workspaces
Redact secrets before handing artifacts to Pipecat
Disable external providers in Pipecat for sensitive runs
Review allowlisted egress destinations before deployment
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering at the bridge

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo exposes REST/gRPC APIs and Pipecat supports a shared bus with multiple instances, but neither profile shows unrestricted write to the same filesystem or git state. The overlap is mainly coordination and API access, so direct write conflict is not established. If both are wired to the same mutable resource, conflict risk rises, but that is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external resource without locking
IF Pipecat instances share a bus that mutates state also edited by Argo
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Use optimistic concurrency checks on shared resources
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat’s shared bus can propagate outputs across instances, and Argo can consume API-driven workflow inputs. If Argo-produced artifacts or parameters are treated as authoritative by Pipecat, errors can cascade into downstream speech or agent actions. The pairwise pathway exists, but the profiles do not show fully automated irreversible actions, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards Argo output to an LLM/STT/TTS step without verification
IF downstream automation acts on Pipecat output as if it were ground truth
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat acts on Argo output
Mark Argo outputs as untrusted in the bridge
Log and review high-impact actions triggered by Pipecat
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and policy gates

E_compliance.rationale: Argo handles artifacts and parameters, while Pipecat processes text, audio, video, images, and conversation state and may send them to third-party providers. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated data is routed through Pipecat’s external services. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in Argo artifacts or Pipecat conversation state
IF Pipecat routes that data to a provider with different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to Pipecat
Use only providers with matching residency terms
Disable logging for regulated sessions
Review retention settings on all external services
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing by data class
